body.text: Natural numbers (1, 2, 3, ...) are the counting numbers. Whole numbers add zero (0, 1, 2, 3, ...). Integers extend further to include negative numbers (..., -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, ...) — these are directed numbers, because the sign shows a direction: above or below zero, such as a temperature, or above or below sea level.

For example, a temperature of -5°C is 5 degrees below zero, and an altitude of -100 m means 100 metres below sea level. Directed numbers combine by moving along a number line: -5 + 3 means starting at -5 and moving 3 to the right, landing on -2.

When a calculation mixes operations, follow the hierarchy of operations (BODMAS): Brackets, then Of/Orders (powers), then Division and Multiplication (left to right), then Addition and Subtraction (left to right). Work out 3 + 4 x (6 - 2): first the bracket gives 6 - 2 = 4, then the multiplication gives 4 x 4 = 16, then the addition gives 3 + 16 = 19.

A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself (2, 3, 5, 7, 11, ...). A composite number has more than two factors. Every composite number can be broken down into a unique product of prime factors — for 60: 60 = 2 x 30 = 2 x 2 x 15 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 5, so 60 = 2² x 3 x 5.

The Highest Common Factor (HCF) of two numbers is the largest number that divides both exactly; the Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) is the smallest number that both divide into exactly. Using prime factors, the HCF takes the lowest power of each shared prime, and the LCM takes the highest power of every prime that appears. For 60 = 2² x 3 x 5 and 42 = 2 x 3 x 7: HCF = 2 x 3 = 6, and LCM = 2² x 3 x 5 x 7 = 420.
